content:
Talia Benson: kicking off Kernel auto-selection v2 thread here so we don’t lose decisions in random DMs. owners / initial Qs esp around model-family taxonomy + seq buckets. core goal: stable p95 across GPUs + no surprises when new model families show up.

Talia Benson: current proposed owners (pls confirm):
- model family detection: @Grace Kim + @Noah Patel
- seq bucket signal / scheduler wiring: @Lena Fischer + @Omar El-Sayed
- GPU sku normalization: @Yuki Sato
- perf suite + baseline: @Marcus Reed + @Rina Kobayashi
- conformance: @Anika Gupta
- release/rollout: @Connor O'Brien
- config/flags/overrides: @Benji Okafor

Hiro Tanaka: :thumbsup: confirmed on Grace/Yuki for selection logic + GPU behavior. I’ll stay looped for review + kernel team capacity.

Grace Kim: confirmed. first question: what’s the source of truth for “model family” today? we have some scattered model metadata but no consistent taxonomy.

Noah Patel: today it’s basically heuristic string matching in a couple places (model name contains “llama”, “mistral”, etc) + some hardcoded flags. it’s brittle.

Sofia Ivanova: for scheduling side: we can emit a “prefill vs decode” phase signal reliably. “effective seq length” is trickier because you don’t know full decode length upfront.

Omar El-Sayed: yeah. at runtime boundary we know:
- prompt_tokens (prefill)
- current_decode_step (for streaming decode)
- max_new_tokens requested
- batch size + padding
we can bucket off prompt_tokens for prefill. for decode maybe use current context length (prompt + generated_so_far) as it grows.

Lena Fischer: scheduler can provide `phase=prefill|decode` and `context_tokens_estimate` (prompt+generated_so_far). might need to be careful about cardinality if we log raw token counts.

Allison Grant: +1 please bucket. do NOT tag metrics with exact seq len.

Grace Kim: proposal for taxonomy: `family` = (arch + key attention flags) not just marketing name. e.g.
- llama-family (llama/llama2/llama3 style)
- mistral-family
- qwen-family
and include key flags like GQA/MQA, rope scaling, sliding window, etc.

Yuki Sato: for GPU side: please don’t key on “A100” string directly. we’ll normalize to something like `gpu_class` + SM capability + memory bw tiers. MIG complicates too.

Noah Patel: +1. also we need unknown families to be safe: default to “safe kernel set” even if slower.

Anika Gupta: on correctness: if selector can choose kernels that have known NaN edge cases at certain shapes, we need guardrails. I’d like a “safe list” that conformance tests cover and selector can fall back to.

Marcus Reed: perf suite can cover top shapes + seq buckets but we need to agree on bucket boundaries. are we thinking like [0-512], [513-2k], [2k-8k], [8k+]? and separate for prefill vs decode?

Grace Kim: I was thinking decouple:
- phase: prefill vs decode
- seq_bucket for prefill based on prompt tokens
- seq_bucket for decode based on context tokens (prompt+generated)
But we should keep buckets coarse to avoid explosion.

Logan Wright: from telemetry POV: recommended labels:
- selector_version (v1/v2)
- kernel_id (hashed/short)
- model_family (coarse)
- seq_bucket (coarse)
- gpu_class (coarse)
No model_name, no exact seq.

Talia Benson: ok. initial open questions list:
1) model family taxonomy: what’s the minimal set for v1 of registry? (llama/mistral/qwen + “unknown”?)
2) seq buckets: boundaries + definitions for prefill/decode
3) how to map model metadata -> family deterministically
4) what info runtime needs from scheduler to choose kernels w/o huge wiring

Connor O'Brien: release side: please design with feature flag + deterministic fallback to v1. we need a hard kill switch during canary.

Benji Okafor: config wise: can do precedence like:
1) emergency kill switch (global)
2) per-model-family override
3) selector v2 table
4) fallback to selector v1
Will add validation that override kernel exists for gpu_class.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler signal can be added behind a flag too so we can test without changing behavior for existing runtime.

Rina Kobayashi: for benchmarks: need representative prompt distributions. if we only do short prompts we’ll overfit. can we get a histogram from prod? (coarse bins)

Omar El-Sayed: we can export a weekly histogram of prompt_tokens + max_new_tokens (bucketed) per top model family. should be fine privacy-wise.

Allison Grant: make sure it’s aggregated and no request-level sampling that could leak. bucket counts only.

Grace Kim: question on “family”: are we ok treating llama2 vs llama3 same family? attention kernels differ if GQA params differ.

Noah Patel: I’d model it as `family_id` + `variant_flags`. e.g. family=llama, flags={gqa=true, head_dim=128, rope=scaled}. but we can keep “flags” limited to what affects kernel choice. otherwise we’ll fragment.

Yuki Sato: +1 keep it to flags that actually change supported kernels / perf. for GPU, I’ll propose classes: L4, A10, A100, H100, plus “other_sm80”, “other_sm90” maybe.

Marcus Reed: on buckets, can we align with known kernel crossovers? e.g. flash-attn vs xformers style tends to flip around 2k-4k depending on GPU.

Hiro Tanaka: yes but we should base on measured thresholds per gpu_class. for now pick conservative boundaries and adjust via table entries later.

Anika Gupta: please ensure boundary definitions are stable (no off-by-one surprises). I’d like unit tests for bucket assignment.

Lena Fischer: ack. we’ll define buckets in one shared module and use in both telemetry + selection.

Talia Benson: action items (today):
- @Grace Kim / @Noah Patel: draft model family taxonomy proposal (top 3 families + unknown) + mapping rules
- @Omar El-Sayed / @Lena Fischer: propose seq bucket scheme for prefill/decode + what scheduler emits
- @Yuki Sato: propose gpu_class normalization mapping (incl MIG notes)
- @Marcus Reed / @Rina Kobayashi: baseline perf run plan (what models + gpu matrix)

Linear: Talia Benson created Linear project ENG-3921 "Kernel auto-selection v2" and linked tasks: ENG-3922, ENG-3923, ENG-3924, ENG-3925.

Grace Kim: I’ll start a doc + share here. quick strawman families for registry v1:
- llama_family
- mistral_family
- qwen_family
- unknown_family (safe kernels only)
then extend later.

Noah Patel: pls include “how to handle finetunes” (e.g. `llama-3-8b-instruct-acme`) - should map to same family based on arch metadata not name.

Omar El-Sayed: seq bucket strawman:
- prefill_prompt_tokens: [0-256], [257-1024], [1025-4096], [4097+]
- decode_context_tokens (prompt+generated_so_far): [0-1024], [1025-4096], [4097-8192], [8193+]
phase emitted separately.

Sofia Ivanova: those seem ok. we can compute context_tokens precisely at each decode step. for selection, do we re-evaluate per step or only once?

Grace Kim: for decode kernels, likely ok to pick once per request and keep stable. reselecting mid-stream would be weird for perf analysis + might cause warmup hits.

Noah Patel: agree. pick at start of decode (first decode step) using initial context length and assume it stays in same bucket. if it crosses a boundary mid-gen, we can ignore for now.

Logan Wright: telemetry should record both:
- bucket_at_selection
- bucket_current (optional)?? careful though.
I’d prefer just bucket_at_selection to keep it clean.

Allison Grant: +1 only log at selection time.

Connor O'Brien: +1 determinism matters. fewer moving parts during canary.

Yuki Sato: fyi MIG: same SKU can show up as “A100-SXM4-40GB MIG 1g.5gb” etc. I’ll normalize MIG to base gpu_class + partition profile in a separate field, but selector should key on base gpu_class unless we see perf issues.

Anika Gupta: for conformance tests we should include at least one run per gpu_class + per bucket for each family. otherwise we’ll miss shape-specific NaNs.

Marcus Reed: noted. perf suite can’t do exhaustive but conformance can be smaller (few prompts per bucket) focusing on numerical sanity.

Talia Benson: thanks. pls drop drafts in this thread by EOD tomorrow. we’ll review in runtime sync Wed.

Grace Kim: :thumbsup:

Omar El-Sayed: :thumbsup:

Yuki Sato: :thumbsup:

Noah Patel: :thumbsup:
